legend: Find the number of different strings of length k$$$k$$$ that you can get by concatenating prefixes of a given string S$$$S$$$.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line of input contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤2000$$$1 \leq t \leq 2000$$$)  — the number of test cases. The description of test cases follows.
The first line contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ (1≤n≤k≤2000$$$1 \leq n \leq k \leq 2000$$$)  — the length of S$$$S$$$ and the size of the desired strings.
The second line contains a string S$$$S$$$ consisting of n$$$n$$$ lowercase letters. It is guaranteed that the sum of k$$$k$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 2000$$$2000$$$.
output: For each test case, print a line with one integer  — the answer to the problem. Since the answer may be huge, print it modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$.
